one_line: An anonymous Yadava-period temple architect and master stone mason of the Deccan, crafting Hemadpanti black-basalt shrines.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, lean but strong, wiry craftsman’s build with ropey forearms and calloused hands.
appearance.face: Oval face with a medium-brown Deccan complexion, straight nose, sharp cheekbones, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, a small white sandalwood tilak on the forehead, default expression focused and calm with a slight, satisfied half-smile as if visualizing a temple plan.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair pulled tightly into a small, low knot at the back of the head (konda) with a simple dull-bronze hairpin, a plain un-dyed off-white cotton headscarf folded narrow and tied around the crown like a band, leaving the knot visible at the back.
appearance.costume: A modest, era-accurate Deccan craftsman outfit: an ankle-length, soft cotton dhoti in muted off-white wrapped firmly in a carpenter’s style with a double-folded front pleat and narrow tuck at the waist, paired with a long-sleeved, collarless cotton angarkha-tunic in dusty slate-grey that reaches mid-thigh and ties with inner and outer cloth ties, the sleeves rolled neatly to just below the elbows; over one shoulder, a narrow ochre-brown cotton uttariya (shawl) with a subtle darker-brown woven border draped diagonally across the chest and wrapped once around the waist like a working sash; bare feet in simple dark-brown leather sandals with a toe loop; minimal jewellery: a single thin copper bangle on the right wrist and small, plain copper stud earrings; all fabrics look handwoven, slightly textured, and practical rather than ornate, with no fancy embroidery, suited to a working architect overseeing a stone yard.
appearance.signature: A wooden measuring staff and set-square combined: a waist-height dark-wood staff with carved notches for units, a small bronze plumb-bob hanging from the top by a cotton cord, and a triangular wooden set-square lashed near the base, which he often rests lightly against his shoulder.

ref_desc: Yadava Sthapati is a mid-30s, medium-brown Deccan man with an oval face, small tilak, short beard, black hair in a low knot with an off-white headband, wearing an off-white dhoti, slate-grey angarkha, ochre-brown sash, simple sandals, and carrying a dark-wood measuring staff-set-square with bronze plumb-bob.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of a dignified Yadava-period temple architect from the Deccan: a mid-30s, lean, medium-brown man with an oval face, sharp cheekbones, straight nose, neat short beard and moustache, and a small white sandalwood tilak on his forehead, his thick black hair pulled into a small low knot at the back secured with a dull-bronze pin and wrapped with a narrow off-white cotton headband tied around the crown. Show him in a modest, historically grounded craftsman’s outfit: an ankle-length off-white handwoven cotton dhoti wrapped firmly with a double-folded front pleat, a long-sleeved slate-grey cotton angarkha-tunic reaching mid-thigh and tied at the side with cloth ties, its sleeves rolled to just below the elbows, and a narrow ochre-brown cotton uttariya draped diagonally over one shoulder and wrapped once at the waist like a working sash. Put simple dark-brown leather sandals with toe loops on his feet and give him minimal jewellery: a thin copper bangle on his right wrist and small plain copper stud earrings. In his hand and resting against his shoulder, show his signature dark-wood measuring staff combined with a triangular wooden set-square lashed near the base and a small bronze plumb-bob hanging by a cord from the top. Use a grounded palette of off-white, slate grey, ochre brown, dark brown, and bronze, and present him front and slight-angle views to clearly show his consistent face, hair, costume, and tool from head to toe.
